results.controlIntent: (a) Set up and administer privileged user accounts in accordance with [Selection: a role-based access scheme; an attribute-based access scheme]; (b) Monitor assignments of privileged roles or attributes; (c) Monitor changes to roles or attributes; and (d) Revoke access when privileged role or attribute assignments are no longer appropriate.

judgment.rationale:
Evidence from both the IAM execution role and CloudTrail events reveals multiple failures across all four sub-requirements of AC-2(7).v1:

**(a) Role-based/attribute-based access scheme — FAILED:** The endpoint's execution role (`SageMakerExecutionRole-Generic`, ARN: `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/SageMakerExecutionRole-Generic`) carries two wildcard policies: `s3:*` on all resources (`*`) and `sagemaker:*` on all resources (`*`). This is the antithesis of a least-privilege, role-based scheme. The role name itself ("Generic") signals it is not purpose-scoped to this model.

**(b) Monitor assignments of privileged roles/attributes — INSUFFICIENT CONTROLS:** No evidence of monitoring mechanisms (AWS Config rules, IAM Access Analyzer, periodic access reviews) for role assignments was returned. The overly broad policies have apparently persisted without detection or remediation.

**(c) Monitor changes to roles or attributes — FAILED:** CloudTrail shows that `data-scientist-jdoe` (an IAM user) created the endpoint (`CreateEndpoint`, 2025-12-01T11:00:00Z) **two hours before** the registry approval at 09:00, and later performed an `UpdateEndpoint` (2026-03-15T14:22:00Z) for a hotfix with **no corresponding registry entry**. These events demonstrate that privileged deployment actions are not being gated or monitored effectively — changes are occurring outside of approved change-control processes.

**(d) Revoke access when no longer appropriate — NO EVIDENCE:** There is no evidence of access revocation processes, periodic reviews, or lifecycle management for the privileged role. The continued presence of wildcard permissions further suggests no revocation or right-sizing has occurred.
gaps: No evidence of IAM Access Analyzer findings or AWS Config rules monitoring role assignments — human attestation needed to confirm whether out-of-band monitoring exists
No evidence of periodic access reviews or role recertification processes
No evidence of a formal access revocation workflow or offboarding procedure for privileged users
Registry approval timestamps were referenced in CloudTrail notes but the registry approval event itself was not returned — a direct registry audit would strengthen the change-control finding
No evidence of whether data-scientist-jdoe's broad access has been reviewed or is still active

policies.note: Overly broad — training bucket writes and cross-account access not scoped

payload.note: Deployed 2h BEFORE registry approval at 09:00 — change control not satisfied
Hotfix deploy — no corresponding registry entry found
